utterances.text: That's 1322, appendix 1. And if possible, that same appendix that was shown to you by Mr. Zivanovic, could it please be called up on our monitors?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I don't have it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope there will not be any problems about admitting this document into evidence. I don't want to introduce any extra markings on it, just ask for some further clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objections? I don't see any. I would leave it there for the time being and we'll deal with it at the end of the testimony, because it may well be made use of by others. So go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, in your analysis, and in the course of today's testimony, you used the words "radio relay route, radio relay path, radio relay node, radio relay station, intercepting station" so I wish to put a few questions in relation to this map. For example with reference to Vlasenica and Veliki Zep, is that a radio relay route or path or what is it?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I may not have been sufficiently clear, although I don't think the questions themselves called for these explanations. So Trasa is -- or a route is one that goes via various different devices. So a radio relay route, the route goes from Vlasenica via Veliki Zep, Cer and Gucevo to Zvornik. So all of that together is a route. It's similar to roads, for example. What I referred to as a path is between two points. So one path is between Vlasenica-Veliki Zep, a second path is between Veliki Zep and Cer. A third between Cer and Gucevo, and the fourth path between Gucevo and Zvornik. Direction is something that is frequently confused with a path, but on the Vlasenica-Veliki Zep, when we call it a direction, that means we have to mention the frequencies, the azimuth and so on. It involves different information. If we refer to it as a path we are simply referring to the part of the route that goes from point A to point B. A radio relay direction, when we talk about a direction, we have to mention all the different details such as the frequency, azimuth, information pertaining to the antenna and so on and so forth. When we radio relay experts talk to each other, we sometimes call the Vlasenica-Veliki Zep direction which might mean that we are looking from Vlasenica towards Veliki Zep, because only so can we say that the antenna in Vlasenica is oriented towards Veliki Zep. When we refer to it as a path, then it doesn't matter whether we are looking from Vlasenica towards Veliki Zep or the other way round. Did you also ask me --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. I asked you about the nodes and the stations.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it's like this: It wasn't I who introduced these terms. It's according to the rules of communication. The terminal radio relay station is the station within a command where there are requirements or needs to establish radio relay communications. This is all concentrated here. Getting information in the direction of Veliki Zep, which is where the end users are. So the place where the end users are, that's the terminal radio relay station. Veliki Zep is a node. There would be no need for it to exist if one could transmit from Vlasenica to Zvornik directly. But as geography does not allow it, you need to have these nodes established for reasons of optical visibility so that you can reach one terminal radio relay station from the other terminal radio relay station. So the reason they are called nodes is that telephone channels from various directions cross here. It's like a junction or a crossing. So it is a crossing of various telephone channels coming from different directions, and RRU, RRU-800, SMC and so on. When there is no need for channels to cross, then the packet of channels that arrives from one direction is simply transmitted through multiplex to another, all the channels are packed and they go on -- go further. That's in an intermediate station. There is no need for telephone channels to cross here at stations. There is only an official link.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in the army of Republika Srpska there were some channels that were protected, some links that were protected?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: That is a more modern type of radio relay, in terms of generations. It's digital and as it's digital, group crypto protection can be introduced at various radio relay directions, from the -- from one end user to another. There was cryptographic protection for the communication. This is a combined system and in this particular case in the Army of Republika Srpska, as in the whole of the Army of Yugoslavia, what was there, because it was inherited, we had Siemens relay equipment, and the encryption and multiplex devices were Swiss-made as was another part of the equipment so that cryptographic protection had to be there from one end user to another. It could not be broken for any reason. According to my documents, there is not a single transcript showing that communications carried out according to this system had been intercepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that the command of the Main Staff, its commander, the Chief of Staff, and corps commanders used these kind of communications, the president of the republic used -- also used encrypted communications? Do you know about this?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I know in principle who was able to have such communications. The same principle applied in Republika Srpska that had applied in Yugoslavia. It was the highest-ranking and top military and political leaders who used such encrypted communications, because the equipment and the sets were limited. As far as I know, this was used from the Main Staff down to corps level, and exceptionally perhaps at lower levels. I didn't carry out an analysis for the entire army, but only in connection with Veliki Zep because I have the diagram here and my finding is that no such communication line or link was compromised.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: At the beginning, we looked at diagram 18, so I would like to ask you to go back to it now. And could we just zoom in on it a little bit?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: This shows the radio relay route from Vlasenica to Zvornik, with the equipment used for transmission. If you look at it in Vlasenica there was an RRU-800 set, the antenna was directed towards Veliki Zep, and to this was connected a multiplex-type device, 24, which means that this direction could have up to 24 analog telephone channels. It also shows the frequencies, the transmission frequencies 1 and 2. I've already mentioned the numbers of the frequencies, so I won't repeat them. This direction had its number from the documentation, from the documentation of the Drina Corps, we see that it bears the number 0607. At Veliki Zep, apart from receiving signals from this direction, from the direction of Cer, there was a 1058 radio set with a capacity of 120 telephone channels, and the multiplex V 120.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Here, the channels at the level of channels, at the level of one participant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Rodic, please slow down because the interpreters are not catching up with you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. The lines from both directions could be combined, channel to channel, according to the plan for communications of the Main Staff and the Drina Corps. At the same time, I showed here the RRU-1. In preparation I did not determine the end location because there was more than one. These locations changed according to need. That is a tactical level device and communications through it can be established according to a particular situation, and usually they last for as long as the action lasts, and then the direction is changed. There may have been rather long periods when RRU-1 was used for communications for smaller tactical units, but it had one telephone channel which could enter the system so that there was no need to have a direction with RRU-1 towards Vlasenica because it fitted into the system from RRU-800.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you for a moment. On this diagram, can you explain how the encrypted communications were transmitted from the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Well, that's not in this diagram, because I did not analyse encrypted communications. If somebody wants to study them in detail, they are in the diagram of encrypted communications in document (0) 433-6629. What can be seen in connection with the Drina Corps command is that from Veliki Zep towards Vlasenica, if I can see correctly, was direction 0674, with a total capacity of eight telephone channels, which had their own cryptographic protection. These channels could be switched over to, towards the Main Staff or towards other units. One can see who the users were, but my analysis did not concern the encrypted communications. However, I can explain, if you need any further explanation. Let me just add that from Veliki Zep to the Main Staff, communications went by cable, not through the ether. They were wire communications, not air communications. They were completely protected from any possibility of interception.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: And finally, Mr. Rodic, you spent some 30 years serving either in the former JNA or in the federal army. Did you have any experience in that army with intercepting communications and can you tell us who was trained or dealt in intercepting communications?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: In my experience, as regards interception, I did not deal with that. However, when I was designing and setting up communications, I had to investigate whether the communications would cross the border. Let me describe one experience I had when, from Brindisi to Venice, I spent about 10 days on a ship where my team, with experts from the institute examined how information leaked in the direction of Italy. That was sometime in 1987. We were not intercepting or writing down the conversations from the army of Yugoslavia that were leaking out. We were just trying to establish whether it was possible to listen in to our communications from boats on the Adriatic and to correct them so that our communications would not go in the direction of Italy but along the coastline. As I was in the sector for communications, information technology and other electronic communications, I studied these principles so that as far as I was able to understand, the level of expertise needed for somebody to engage in intercepting, what I can say is as follows: In the army of Serbia and also Montenegro towards the end of my service, the conscripts would spend about 12 months in the army. The service for electronic reconnaissance and surveillance received into its ranks only A category soldiers, which meant the men had to be in good health, they had to be intelligent, agile, and have good hearing. Such men were taken to very modern laboratories with the same technology that was actually in use, and they would spend six months there on intensive training. After those six months, they would go to various military units of the corresponding kind and there they would have further practice. At the end of those six months, they were not able to independently carry out complex tasks. They were assigned auxiliary tasks. And when they were called up into the reserves, they were given additional intensive training in order for them to keep up their skills and to be able to intercept conversations at a certain level. However, it was officers or commanders with many years of experience in this specialty who actually intercepted conversations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Petrusic. Mr. Josse?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We do have some cross-examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead. Before you do so, Mr. Sarapa, are you confirming that the Pandurevic Defence team doesn't wish to put any questions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Sarapa. Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: If the Chamber were contemplating a break, I would rather do my cross-examination of a piece, and taking the break now would suit me enormously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How long do you expect your cross-examination to last?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: At least 15 minutes, perhaps 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because we have 15 minutes or 17 minutes now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'll start.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And if you're not finished we'll take another extra five minutes before we break.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, the first thing I'd like to ask you about is something that my learned friend Mr. Petrusic has just cross-examined you or examined you, perhaps I should say, about, and this relates to the communications between the president of the Republika Srpska and the command of the Main Staff. You'd mentioned that these were encrypted communications; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: My task was not to analyse that type of communications. However, based on this diagram, it can be --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Could I -- I'm going to stop you for a --

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: There. I did not go into that because I was not given that sort of task. Here at Veliki Zep, you have one channel for the government of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Could I say, Mr. Rodic, I'm very anxious that you do not stray into areas where you quite properly say you either have not spent sufficient time examining or alternatively you say for one reason or another you don't have sufficient expertise in relation to, so I accept your answer and I'm going to move on to a different topic, if I may.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: If you will allow me to say this, I am an expert in that field but I was not asked to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Thank you. So in other words, if you were given more time, you could research it but you haven't done so for the purpose of your testimony today. That's what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: More time and more documents, or rather documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: There are two other areas that I wish to ask you about, and if your answer is the same, please let the Chamber know. The first of those two areas relates to what we in this case have called Paket communications. Does that it expression mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Do you mean documents of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I used one term, and that was a package of -- a packet of telephone channels, which had to do with the total capacity of telephone channels along those links. Are you referring to the Paket radio in the context of the BH documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I am. Let me show you an example. Could the witness be shown 6D47, please? We've simply called this up as an example of what I'm referring to. It's what you've just described, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: What is the question again?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: This is an example of what you've just described, isn't it, the type of communication that you were just talking about?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I don't understand what your question is in relation to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'd simply called this document up so that everyone could know what I was referring to. I want to ask you about the Paket communication that you have just described.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I did not include Paket communication in my analysis. It's quite a different principle of transmission. In short, my analysis did not refer to Paket communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Were you familiar with Paket communication from your work during the war?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: While I was performing those duties, that sort of Paket communication had not been introduced in the army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Let me ask you another question, and of course, say if you can't answer this. Do you know, for example, where the communication centre was located within the Srebrenica enclave, the centre of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: No. I don't know that. Had I known this piece of information and the frequencies, I would have processed it in my report. I didn't know the end point or the frequencies used for that communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Right. I'll try my luck with my third line of examination, and it's this: You were briefed to examine --

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I'm not receiving anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So we may have a problem. Madam Usher, could you just give first aid first and then we see --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps we could take the break. I would now appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll have a 25-minute break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: The break has proved very fruitful and on reflection, I'm going to abandon the third line of cross-examination and I'm going to sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That concludes the -- that concludes the cross-examination -- the examination-in-chief and one cross-examination. Mr. Vanderpuye, have you distributed the list of documents that you intended to use?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I believe I have, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I hope that the Defence teams don't just believe they have it but they are certain they do. So let's commence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. Good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And may I ask you how long you expect your cross-examination to last?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I had initially estimated I think about two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I know that the witness has some pressing concerns of his own. I'll try and -- I'll try and come as close to finishing as I can, but I'm not certain that I can in the time that's left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You promise to graduate us from layman to at least mini experts on the subject, take as much time as you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You've put together a very detailed and technical analysis of the possibility of interception, as you've indicated, on the route between Vlasenica and Zvornik. Now, as an expert you have to be neutral. Is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And you also have to be objective in the analysis that you perform, right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And you have to take into consideration very carefully all of the information with which you've been provided, right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the information you were provided with, you also have to scrutinise to determine if it's sufficient in order to draw a conclusion from it, right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Right. Insofar as my expertise permits me to.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You have to also scrutinise the information to determine if it's accurate and reliable, right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: As far as I was able to examine it and as far as the circumstances permitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And of course you have to scrutinise all of that information to determine if it's reliable, right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Insofar as I was able to, given the documentation that I was able to collect under the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you've made several references to the documentation that you've examined in support of the report that you generated. Now, is the documentation that you examined the same documentation that's appended to your report?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: If you're referring to the documentation of the Drina Corps, that's to say of the Main Staff, yes. Is that the documentation you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Maybe I should rephrase the question. I don't think I -- I think I can make it a little clearer. Did you examine any other documentation than the documentation that's included in your report?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: These were the documents that I appended and included in my list and in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. So you've not examined any other documents other than the documents that are included in this report or relied on any other documents other than the documents included in this report; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: They were the documents I examined. There were other documents that I did not consider important for my analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you created this analysis or when you engaged in this analysis, you knew that this was a report that was going to be tendered in this case, right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Of course. I wasn't aware of the full procedure at the time, but I knew it was to be material tendered before a court of law.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So you knew that it carried with it the potential to be relied upon by the Defence counsel, by the Prosecution and even by the Court when you prepared it, right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, the documents that you reviewed, that you've just referred to, were those documents provided to you by Defence counsel or were they documents that you came into on your own?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I didn't obtain any documents on my own, independently, and I'm referring to the documents themselves. Neither did I have any opportunity to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Just so that I'm clear, with respect to the intercepts that you looked at that are included or referenced in your report, those are documents that were provided to you by Defence counsel; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the documents showing the specifications of the equipment that you analysed in relation to the possibility of interception, those were documents -- well, let me ask you: Where did those documents originate? Where did you get them?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: The documents relative to the equipment in possession of the BH army were given to me by the Defence. As for the technical specifications, I collected those myself over the internet.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, the documents showing the VRS communications setup for the route that you analysed, was that a document that was given to you by the Defence as well?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And these are all documents that you relied upon in reaching the conclusions that you drew at the end of your report; is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The documents that are appended to your report are documents that you relied on in reaching the conclusions that you made about the possibility of interception by the ABiH army, right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. The documents, I said originated from the command of the Drina Corps and the Main Staff. May I state the number of documents or the number of the document? Is it necessary?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think you can. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: This is document in appendix 12, number 04314791.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, you know -- sorry, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: In appendix 13, 04314792. In appendix 14, 0426990, and in appendix 15, 0426703, and in appendix 16, 04336628.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you know as an expert that even though it may be inevitable, it's important to avoid making assumptions, right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Because you recognise that if you make an incorrect assumption, that could make a technical report such as the one you generated factually erroneous, right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I don't know where it was that I made any assumptions.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Well, I'm just talking in generalities right now, and we'll go to more specific instances a little bit later on. You can agree that if you make an assumption that's incorrect or rely on an assumption that's incorrect, it can result in an error in a technical report, right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: To a certain extent, yes, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it can also result in a theoretical flaw in a technical report, right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Would you agree that it's a better practice and more accurate when you're making a technical report to rely on facts that can be established or substantiated than it is to rely on an assumption?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Right. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you're generating a technical report and you do rely on an assumption, can we agree that it's important to identify what that assumption is?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's also important to have evaluated the assumption itself, to see if it's reasonable under the circumstances, right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it's also important to indicate in the report itself the extent to which an assumption underlies a given conclusion, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in this case, when you generated the report, that's what you tried to do, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So you checked to make sure that the assumptions that you made were reasonable, right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I believe they are reasonable.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you checked to make sure that the assumptions that you relied upon could be substantiated, right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. I will try to substantiate them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think you indicated at the very beginning of your testimony that the objective of your analysis was to assess the possibility of interception along the Vlasenica-Zvornik route during the period of June through August of 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you --

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sorry. You were hired by the Defence to provide an opinion about that possibility; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So if I understand your report, and I probably -- I'm going to make a lot of mistakes about it because it's very technical, but if I understand it, your report is limited strictly to this objective, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So you didn't consider the possibility of interception along other radio relay routes; is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Only for the ones that I indicated. They were the objective.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, aside from the routes themselves, you didn't consider the possibility of frequencies corresponding to routes other than the ones that you examined when you analysed the documents; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Can you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Maybe I can put it in a bit of context for you. I think when you were asked on direct examination whether or not there was a possibility of interception, you indicated that one of the reasons there wasn't was because the frequencies didn't correspond to the existing plan; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So my question is, did you consider the possibility that the frequencies might correspond to other routes?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I was interested in the route that was given to me as an assignment. I did not consider the entire network or in the general area, except for the 630 850, where I said that according to BH Army documents it originated from the Sarajevo area.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, when you say 380, at least that's what the record says, that doesn't correspond to either a RRU-1 or an RRU-800 device; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: 630, not 380 but 630 and 850. One was of 630 megahertz and the other one of 850. It may have been a slip on my part. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying that. I just wanted to make sure it was accurate on the record. You didn't consider the possibility of interception of mobile communications equipment, did you?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: No. That was not my task and I'm not an expert on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: But you do know, in your experience, that an RRU device can be mobile or mobilised?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Which? RRU -- RRU-1 or 800?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: RRU-1 and RRU-800.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I explained that RRU-800 was used for stationary communications systems. It can also be used in a transported communications system in which case it is transported in a cab. As for the RRU-1, I said that it can be carried by a soldier depending on the mobility. It can be dislocated from one point to another. I believe I was quite clear on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, I'm only asking whether or not an RRU-800 is a device that can be moved and operate in a moving, for example, a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: It cannot. It's not a radio set. I was quite clear. I said it was directed communication, and it requires quite a lot of practice to move it from one point, and especially impossible is to do that on a moving vehicle. That's a nonsense. The same goes for RRU-1. If you have a directed antenna, then it constitutes directed communications. It can have a directed antenna. It can operate with that. But with that sort of antenna, you cannot set up a point-to-point communications link, which was my task.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I think that's clear. I'm not sure if I understand it, but I think it's clear. Now, were you aware of any RRU-800 devices that may have been in locations other than the specific locations that you've indicated on the route that you analysed?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I did not analyse that because I had the entire diagram of communications, and I had the tasks that I was given.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the entire diagram of communications you looked at, though, didn't include any RRU-800s that might be mounted on a vehicle, for example, not a vehicle in motion but just mounted on a vehicle. Is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I had the entire diagram of communications and it included stationary elements only.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you would agree, wouldn't you, that the potential existence of such devices, within the context of analysing the possibility of interception of those devices, is something that's relevant to your analysis, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: It's not relevant, when it comes to RRU-800 I was looking at the stationary communications systems operating out of the facilities that were known to have been communications centres. I did not analyse anything that may have been in motion or outside of these facilities. I didn't have information to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the information that you might have had wasn't provided to you; is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I was provided with the information I have included in my analysis. I did not have any other information.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Did you ask for any other information? Did you seek that out?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I could have asked for information but only through the Defence team. As an individual, there was nobody else I could contact in this regard, either in my country or, let's say, the other country. And they will explain how they came by the documents. I'm not going into that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: But you didn't ask the Defence team for those documents or to see if there were such documents at all, did you?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Of course I did, but I can't ask for specific documents as I don't know what documents there are. I was looking for the diagram of the Drina Corps communications system, but I didn't ask for this information in relation to other corps since that was not the object of my study. Nor did I ask about other systems such as radio, Paket radio, if they had it because again that was not my task.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, you have a lot of experience in analysing and maybe even designing radio relay communications systems; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: A great deal of experience in -- and great understanding in how those communications work and the devices that are involved in that communication system, right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Well, with respect to the technology used in my generation, yes, I think so. I don't have all the technical details at my fingertips but the analysis, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, so you know that if an RRU-800 device can be integrated into a stationary system, that's something that's worth considering in determining whether or not an interception can occur on that line; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question. Could you please repeat it? I don't see what you're getting at.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You know that an RRU-800 device can communicate within the stationary system that you analysed, right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it doesn't have to be a stationary RRU-800 device that communicates with -- within that system?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: It doesn't have to be stationary, but in this case, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: There were facilities where that device was located. Even if the device were on a vehicle, in the cabin of the vehicle, but it's at the command where it's being used, it can stand there for months or years, and then it's stationary. It doesn't matter whether it's on wheels or in a room.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if it can stay there for months or years, then it means it can move from one place to another during that time, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: No, because there is no communication then left for that command.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I mean is that -- I'm sorry, finish your answer.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: If one device is providing communications for a particular command, the device is dislocated, but the command is not, that would mean that the command would have no means of communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, have you ever in your experience known a command to move from one location to another?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, when a command moves and it's connected by an RRU-800 device that's in a cab or a vehicle, what happens to the cab or the vehicle with the RRU-800 device? Is it left where it was or does it go with the command?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Of course it goes with the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So if the command moves from one place to another in a period of, say, about two years, it's possible that an RRU-800 device attached to the command would move with it, right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Which means it might not be in the same place as it was two years prior, right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: As a rule, yes, but in my analysis, it was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I think I heard you say during the course of your direct testimony that you actually went to Veliki Zep at some point during August of 1995; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Mid-August, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And during that period of time, you had an opportunity to evaluate the equipment that was being used there. Was that the purpose of your visit?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Not to evaluate the equipment but to improve the situation, not only that facility but in other facilities in the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you say improve the situation, what exactly do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: We had a team equipped with the appropriate instruments and some reserve parts, and to the best of our ability, we improved the quality of communication on the radio relay paths. Up to that point, the quality was -- well, it had been very bad, because there was no money to buy spare parts, the experts in the former Yugoslavia had been located in the large centres, so that some commands were left without the appropriate equipment or reserve parts, so our aim was to improve this situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think you also indicated that there was an SMC line that runs along the route from Veliki Zep to Cer; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I didn't only indicate that, but as I mentioned twice I serviced it on two occasions, once when it was shelled and it didn't exist any more -- well, actually, three times. The first time it was set up, I was not then at Veliki Zep but on the opposite side, at Cer, when the Cer- Veliki Zep communication was redirected, because before that it was operated according to another plan through Zlovrh, which was, which the BH Army had taken and it couldn’t any more… there were no conditions for that path to be used… but I wasn't at Veliki Zep. I was at Cer then.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And when was that, so we are clear?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I don't know what the date is. You might be able to check when Zlovrh was taken by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I have forgotten the time exactly, the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And when you were -- well, when you were in Veliki Zep, was that in August of 1995? That is correct, right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was the last time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And while you were there, did you service that line? I think you mentioned you did that a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Primarily we fixed those 120-channel paths because they were the most important ones and then also the 24-channel ones with the RRU-800.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And how long were you at that facility in August of 1995 fixing those parts?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I think we completed that in two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Before you arrived there, did you get any information as to how long the problem had existed with those parts?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: We were not given information about problems only that facility but the entire network. So we made a plan and went from one facility to the next. So we didn't go there only because of Veliki Zep but also because of Kozara, Klekovaca, and other radio relay nodes, Banja Luka, Kmur.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. So there were problems that were pervasive within the system of communications; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were problems. For example, there was a double transmitter and a receiver, SMC, which had to be repaired to the best of our ability, but we didn't have spare parts. As for RRU-800, there were bad connections of the antenna systems which had been corroded by rain. That was a tube, not a transistor, and the tubes were almost unusable. We had some spare parts, so we made a plan to improve the most important routes as best we could.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just so I'm clear, before you went to Veliki Zep in August, 1995, you didn't have any information as to how long the SMC line had had problems; is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Let me repeat: We went all over the network and we ourselves found where the problems were, to remove them. It wasn't that we were invited especially to Veliki Zep, because it was a lengthy process that we were in, not just there. We also went to the Republic of Srpska Krajina, and after that we arrived in the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in preparing your analysis in this particular case, you haven't -- you haven't had an opportunity to go back to Veliki Zep or to Cer or to any other node that's involved in your analysis; is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: No, I did not. I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So you haven't had any field measurements that have been taken with respect to the possibility of interception, which is the subject matter of your report?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, not only that but some other things were not possible with regards to technical investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, is one of the things that wasn't possible the opportunity to examine the equipment that was actually involved during this period of time?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The period of time that --

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: You mean when I was doing my analysis, preparing the report? No, not a chance, because I have not been a member of the army for three years now, three and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, I see you've done a lot of calculations, but did you have an opportunity to conduct any tests of the same type of equipment that was used back in 1995, which is the subject matter of your report?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: When preparing my analysis, you mean, for the purpose of my analysis?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: For the purpose of your analysis, that's right.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you carry out any particular tests by way of computer modelling programmes in order to determine whether or not your calculations are accurate or the equipment could be used in a way that it was claimed to have been used?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you aware of any such programmes, by the way, sir?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I have never had any such computer programmes in my experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So you're unaware that such programmes exist?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Well, to be quite honest, I don't understand your question. I don't know what you're asking me about.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. In your consideration of the documents that are included or referenced in your report, you didn't consider the factual content of the intercepts themselves; is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't consider the factual content. I was interested in the possibility of intercepting, that is the frequencies, the devices used, the kind of antenna used. That's the level I was interested in. I wasn't interested in the content.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So you never analysed anything like statements or testimony of anybody who has any knowledge about this type of equipment?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: You mean equipment used for intercepting?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Can you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The equipment used for intercepting, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you can be specific with the witness, I think it would help, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you ask for any information concerning what was claimed with respect to how the intercepting equipment was used, of Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us what, if anything, you learned as a result of that question?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you ask to see the statements of any of the operators that claimed to have intercepted communications from the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you consider the possibility that that information may be relevant or helpful to your analysis as to the possibility of intercepting VRS communications along the route that you analysed?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I relied only on the documents where the intercepters were describing or commenting how they were doing their intercepts, what their problems were, their comments on the quality and so on. But not their statements. I did not have occasion to hear their statements or their testimonies. I saw a map that they generated concerning the connections they intercepted. That was two days ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, that map isn't obviously, I guess, included in your report, right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: No, it couldn't have been because I submitted my report long ago and secondly I would not have taken it into consideration anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Although it does confirm some of what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, having seen the map, does it confirm the location of the intercept sites that you've indicated in your report exist?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: That map does not cover the intercepting centres but only the facilities of the army of Republika Srpska around Zepa, the Drina Corps area, and there are many imprecisions in it. I might be able to comment on the map if you were to show it to me, although I don't attach any great significance to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- well, one of the conclusions you drew in your report was that based on an analysis of the documents that you saw, it appeared as though the ABH army did not have an understanding of the communications system that you analysed; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, did you compare that against the map that you saw a couple of days ago?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did that map contain locations such as Veliki Zep?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: It -- the locations were there, but I reached my conclusions before I had the map, and secondly, as an intercepter, I would not establish the azimuths of intercepting in any direction but Veliki Zep, and according to their documents, they did not do this. So my conclusion was that they were not aware of the largest facility. You can see the angles they worked with, from the northern and southern intercepting station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. I think that on page 75, line 11, there is an omission in the interpretation, because he said that the location was there but was not entered into -- in correctly, and that was omitted in the interpretation, at least so it seemed to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Obviously, I didn't hear that. So if the witness can confirm it. What did you say exactly? You were asked, "And did the map contain locations such as Veliki Zep?" What was the first part of your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My answer was that the location of Veliki Zep is marked on the map, but the location of Vlasenica is not where it is purported to be in that map. Neither is the Zvornik location. It corresponds to what I see in my documentation, that the SMC route Veliki Zep-Cer is functioning, that there is the Cer-Gucevo route, the Gucevo-Zvornik route.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Vanderpuye, because you've got very little time left.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. You say that the indication on that map, on that map, Vlasenica isn't in the right place; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: The way the symbol on the radio relay station is drawn in, no. If they thought it was there, it wasn't. I'd like to see the map because now I'm referring to it on the basis of my recollection. I did not use that map to make my analysis so I don't remember every detail in it. I might be able to indicate other things in it. For example, there was an SMC route drawn in which never actually was in operation, and you can see that. There is their frequency, which has been entered into the map, from Gucevo towards Zvornik, but they don't have it in their intercepts.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. So you did see in that map the locations Vlasenica, wrong as it may be, Veliki Zep --

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Judging by the symbol, although -- well, they used the symbol for the terminal radio relay station, but there was no communication centre there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. You saw the location Cer marked on that map?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: That map is very bad, but I think that location is there, and it corresponds to the actual situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Crni Vrh, did you see that there on the map?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I did, but that map is not very clear. So I don't know whether it's on the peak or whether it's dislocated, but there is the Gucevo-Crni Vrh location there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Could I have 65 ter number 1468, please, on the screen? I will preface this by saying it's not on my exhibit list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Where is Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I just want to confirm which map it is he saw. That's the whole purpose of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have the hard copy here? Perhaps you can -- I know the one. I mean, you don't need to --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's coming up, anyway. It's coming up. Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the map that we showed the expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps you can show it to him as well while it comes up, because it's going to take all our time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That would actually be preferable if he could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Show it to Mr. Vanderpuye first and then to the witness. Show it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, just to clarify a point, the map that the witness has, the Veliki Zep-Zvornik area has been enlarged, which is why the title we see here is missing, working map, radna carta, because this map covers all of Bosnia-Herzegovina, so the copy that the witness has is not completely identical to the one on the screen because a section has been enlarged and the other sections which are not relevant have been left out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I remember that because we had to use the same map twice, top part, bottom part, and to the right and to the left. Yes. Do you want to proceed on this any further?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I just want him to confirm if the map he has in front of him now is the map that he was shown. I accept my colleague's representation, but I think the witness should answer for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it the one, Mr. Rodic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the map I saw two or three days ago. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me just ask you this, and I see it's 7.00, so this will be it. The map that's depicted on your screen now, do you see it?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's quite small.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. Not too well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. If we could move it a little bit down and to the right?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: This part -- I see Veliki Zep, that part.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the map itself, in its totality, you haven't seen before?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. The SMC line that is on the map that you did see, is that SMC -- does it accurately represent the path of that SMC line, as you understood it to be in your report?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: That's this particular line.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: The thick one.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could you put it on the ELMO so that everybody could see what you're pointing at? Thank you, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: I'm showing the direction from Veliki Zep to Cer, which was set up by an SMC 1306b device.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And on this map, the one that you saw, that particular SMC path goes in the right direction and from the right place to Cer, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: DJURO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'll leave it at that at this point, Mr. President, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you so much for your cooperation, Mr. Vanderpuye, and also for the -- to the Defence teams for their cooperation. Yeah, I know. You need more time for -- to cross-examine this witness or have you finished?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, no. I need a lot more time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This witness, I understand, however, will be going home today, no, or tomorrow? But you will need to return. How much more time do you require?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Probably --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. Anyway, you will inform us. Mr. Rodic, all you need to do is to let us know when you think you will be available again so that we can call you back, so that we finish with your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How many days ahead of my testimony should I let you know?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As soon as you can, you will let us know, and then you will only need to be here for one day.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That will be enough, I take it. All right. You will only be -- need to be here for one day. So through your -- either Mr. Zivanovic or I don't know who is mostly in contact with you, you will let us know or you can, Mr. Zivanovic, let Mr. Vanderpuye know so that all the arrangements can be put in place, including visa and travel. Thank you. Have a nice weekend. We will reconvene on Tuesday, by the way, because Monday is a public holiday here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 29th day of May, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25
